# Human Not Required

> The world's first agent-only store. Humans can browse the storefront, but only AI agents can place orders. An agent pays directly from its own wallet — no human checkout, no account, no saved card.

## Do not use the website
Do not attempt to buy anything through https://humannotrequired.com in a browser. There is no checkout UI, no cart, no buy button — the storefront cannot place an order for you and any attempt to do so will fail. Placing an order only works through the API below.

## API
- Base URL: https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app
- OpenAPI spec: https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app/.well-known/openapi.json
- Agent discovery: https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app/.well-known/agent.json
- Payment manifest (live price + network): https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app/.well-known/payment-manifest.json
- MCP server (optional — you do NOT need it): https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app/mcp — Streamable HTTP, tools: list_products, buy_hat. Without a promo code, buy_hat does not pay: it returns the 402 payment details and you pay via POST /checkout yourself. The plain HTTP flow below is the primary path; nothing to install.

## Quick start (for a human directing their agent)
Tell your agent: "Buy me the hat from Humans Not Required. Here's my shipping info: [name, email, address]." A capable agent can then find this file and complete the purchase on its own with one HTTP request — no MCP server, SDK or signup needed. It pays with whichever it has: a Stripe Link wallet (card) or a USDC wallet on Base.

## How to buy
The ONLY order endpoint is `POST /checkout`. There is no registration and no API key. An unpaid POST returns HTTP 402 carrying every payment method currently offered. Three ways to pay:

### Pay with x402 (USDC on Base — fully agent-native)
Requires: an EVM wallet on Base with USDC, and any x402 v2 client (e.g. @x402/fetch).
1. POST /checkout with { sku, name, email, address } and Content-Type: application/json — with no payment header.
2. Server returns 402 with a `Payment-Required` response header (base64 JSON, x402 v2) carrying `accepts[]`.
3. Agent signs an EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` for the USDC amount and retries the same request with the payment header (`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` for x402 v2, or `X-PAYMENT` for v1).
4. USDC settles on Base and the hat ships automatically. No human involvement ever.
- Read the live network, USDC contract, amount, and payee from the 402 envelope (or the payment manifest) — never hard-code them. The store runs Base Sepolia (testnet) by default and flips to Base mainnet for production pricing.
- Payment is captured only after /checkout returns 2xx. A 502 (`fulfillment_failed`) means no USDC was captured — safe to retry. Idempotency is keyed on the payment nonce: replaying the same signed authorization returns your original order, not a second hat.

### Pay with a Stripe Link wallet (card, via Stripe's Machine Payments Protocol)
Offered when the 402 includes `WWW-Authenticate: Payment ... method="stripe"`.
1. `link-cli mpp pay https://web-production-77376.up.railway.app/checkout -X POST -d '<body>'` (Stripe's @stripe/link-cli). Your human approves the spend in the Link app.
2. The client retries with `Authorization: Payment <credential>` carrying a Shared Payment Token; the server charges it through Stripe and returns 201 with a `Payment-Receipt` header.
- Same body and validation as x402. The price is in the challenge (`request` param); it can differ from the USDC price — trust the 402, not this page. One payment token = one charge = one hat: re-sending the same token returns your original order.
- If fulfillment fails after the charge, the payment is refunded automatically (502 `fulfillment_failed`).

### Pay with a promo code (free)
1. POST /checkout with { sku, name, email, address, promo_code } and no payment header.
2. A valid code places a free order; an invalid or exhausted code returns 400/409 with no charge.
- Send exactly one of: a promo_code, an x402 payment, or a Stripe MPP credential. Mixing them is rejected as `ambiguous_payment`.

## Available products
- sku: hat-myagent-os — "My Agent Bought Me This" Embroidered Hat — One Size
  - Prices are set server-side per payment method and may differ (e.g. Stripe Link vs USDC). The unpaid 402 from POST /checkout is authoritative for both; the payment manifest lists them too.

## Auth
None. The payment (x402 signature or Stripe MPP credential) IS the authorization. There is no Bearer token and no POST /register.

## Limits
- No human checkout — the storefront has no buy button; only the agent API can order. See "Do not use the website" above.
- Promo attempts are throttled per IP. An optional per-email daily x402 cap can be enabled by the operator (returns 429 when exceeded).

## Store
- Storefront: https://humannotrequired.com
- Built by: @nft_leen
